thing-thakhek-loop.description: Ride Khammouane’s classic 450 km circuit from Thakhek through Cave Alley, the Nakai Plateau, Thalang, the karst corridor and Kong Lor before returning to the Mekong.
thing-thakhek-loop.gettingThere: Start and finish in Thakhek; most travellers rent a motorbike in town
thing-thakhek-loop.bestTime: Cool dry season; start each riding day early and avoid riding after dark

thing-kong-lor-cave.description: Take a local longtail boat through Kong Lor’s roughly 7.5 km underground river, crossing the limestone mountain to the Natane side before returning through the darkness.
thing-kong-lor-cave.gettingThere: Classic Thakhek Loop stop via Khoun Kham / Kong Lor village
thing-kong-lor-cave.bestTime: Early morning in the drier season; confirm river conditions

thing-tham-nang-aen-cave.description: Walk through Nang Aen’s huge developed limestone chambers just off Route 12, with cool cave air, stairways, coloured lighting and an optional underground-river boat extension.
thing-tham-nang-aen-cave.gettingThere: About 18 km northeast of Thakhek via Route 12, then the signed access road
thing-tham-nang-aen-cave.bestTime: Morning for fewer visitors; especially useful as a cool stop in hot weather

thing-tham-xiang-liap-cave.description: Follow Route 12 to Xiang Liap, a natural river cave near Thakhek where a huge entrance, flowing water and changing seasonal depth shape the visit.
thing-tham-xiang-liap-cave.gettingThere: About 14 km northeast of Thakhek via Route 12 near Xiang Liap village
thing-tham-xiang-liap-cave.bestTime: Dry season for clearer, shallower water; check conditions after rain

thing-tham-chang-elephant-cave.description: Stop at Elephant Cave near Ban Tham for a compact Buddhist shrine visit centred on the golden Buddha, the revered elephant shaped formation and the open view across the plain.
thing-tham-chang-elephant-cave.gettingThere: Follow Route 12 east from Thakhek, then use the local access toward Ban Tham
thing-tham-chang-elephant-cave.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon; check local access after heavy rain

thing-tham-pha-buddha-cave.description: Visit Tham Pa Fa near Thakhek for a sacred cave sanctuary holding 229 bronze Buddha images, rediscovered in 2004 and still approached as an active place of worship.
thing-tham-pha-buddha-cave.gettingThere: About 14 km from Thakhek at Ban Na Khan Sarng
thing-tham-pha-buddha-cave.bestTime: Morning; dress for the shrine and arrive well before the 17:00 closing time

thing-tha-falang.description: Stop beside the Nam Don at Tha Falang for a simple river break between Cave Alley stops, with clear water, shaded banks and swimming when current conditions are suitable.
thing-tha-falang.gettingThere: About 15 km east of Thakhek on Route 12, then a short local track toward the river
thing-tha-falang.bestTime: Dry season for simpler access; quieter on weekdays; check the river after rain

thing-khoun-kong-leng.description: Follow Route 13 north from Thakhek to Khoun Kong Leng, an emerald karst spring near Ban Nakhou where underground water, limestone and local legend define the visit.
thing-khoun-kong-leng.gettingThere: About 50 km from Thakhek via Route 13 and the paved Ban Nakhou access road
thing-khoun-kong-leng.bestTime: Morning in the dry season; check current swimming and water activity rules on arrival

thing-thalang-nam-theun-reservoir.description: End the first Loop day in Thalang, where the Nakai Plateau road meets the Nam Theun 2 reservoir and sunset falls across open water and drowned tree trunks.
thing-thalang-nam-theun-reservoir.gettingThere: Classic Day 1 from Thakhek via Route 12, about 105 km before the overnight stop in Thalang
thing-thalang-nam-theun-reservoir.bestTime: Arrive before sunset and leave early for the 145 km Day 2 ride

thing-pha-inh-cave.description: Make a short Route 12 stop at Pha Inh, a sacred limestone cave where a Buddhist shrine and a naturally lit underground pool create a quieter contrast to the larger Cave Alley sites.
thing-pha-inh-cave.gettingThere: Route 12 east of Thakhek; short side-road approach on the classic Day 1 corridor
thing-pha-inh-cave.bestTime: Morning to midday for stronger natural cave light; follow current local water rules

thing-cool-springs-loop.description: Break up the second Loop day at Cool Springs near Ban Napavan, where cold turquoise spring water sits below limestone and forest after the long ride from Thalang.
thing-cool-springs-loop.gettingThere: On the Thalang–Khoun Kham stage, turn off Route 8 near Ban Napavan and follow the local side track to the pool
thing-cool-springs-loop.bestTime: Late morning or early afternoon for a cooling swim; avoid letting the stop push the ride toward darkness

thing-old-french-railway-bridge.description: Cross from Don Det to Don Khon on the historic railway bridge, then follow traces of the former Mekong portage line by bicycle or on foot.
thing-old-french-railway-bridge.gettingThere: Cross from south Don Det to Don Khon

thing-li-phi-somphamit-waterfalls.description: Ride across Don Khon to Li Phi / Tad Somphamit, where the Mekong breaks into powerful rocky channels and broad white-water rapids.
thing-li-phi-somphamit-waterfalls.gettingThere: About 2 km from the railway bridge on Don Khon

thing-khone-phapheng-falls.description: Leave the islands for the immense Khone Phapheng cataract, combining the Don Det boat crossing with a mainland road transfer to the Mekong viewpoints.
thing-khone-phapheng-falls.gettingThere: Boat to Ban Nakasang, then road transfer

thing-don-som-island.description: Take a local boat north from Don Det to a much quieter Mekong island of villages, rice fields and fishing, with far less tourism infrastructure than Don Det.
thing-don-som-island.gettingThere: Direct local boat from Don Det; arrange the return

thing-khone-pa-soi-waterfall.description: Ride Don Khon's rough eastern tracks to a quieter Mekong waterfall, where the backroad approach, suspension bridge and old timber-route traces are part of the experience.
thing-khone-pa-soi-waterfall.gettingThere: Cross to Don Khon, then follow the eastern tracks by bicycle
thing-khone-pa-soi-waterfall.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon; drier tracks help

thing-xai-kong-nyai-beach.description: Finish a Don Khon ride at a sandy Mekong bank for a cautious swim, simple food and an unhurried break downstream from Li Phi.
thing-xai-kong-nyai-beach.gettingThere: Cross to Don Khon and continue south by bicycle; easy to pair with Li Phi
thing-xai-kong-nyai-beach.bestTime: Late afternoon for cooler air and softer light

thing-si-phan-don-by-boat.description: Leave Don Det in a local pirogue and read Si Phan Don from the water: tiny islands, fishing boats, river crossings and a return through golden-hour Mekong light.
thing-si-phan-don-by-boat.gettingThere: Arrange a private boat at Don Det pier or with a local operator

thing-4000-islands-kayaking.description: Spend a full day paddling the Mekong channels around Si Phan Don on a guided Don Det tour, with moving water and stops built into the route.
thing-4000-islands-kayaking.gettingThere: Book with a Don Det kayak operator; meeting point depends on operator
thing-4000-islands-kayaking.bestTime: Morning departure; follow current river conditions

thing-cycle-don-det-don-khon.description: Rent a simple bicycle on Don Det, follow quiet river and rice-field paths, cross the old railway bridge and keep riding onto Don Khon at your own pace.
thing-cycle-don-det-don-khon.gettingThere: Rent in central Don Det, then ride south to the railway bridge

thing-don-det-tubing.description: Rent an inner tube on Don Det and drift with the Mekong for a simple, low-effort river experience, making the old railway bridge your hard exit point.
thing-don-det-tubing.gettingThere: Rent locally on Don Det and confirm the day's entry and exit points
thing-don-det-tubing.bestTime: Only when current and local advice are suitable

thing-don-det-sunset.description: Walk or cycle to Don Det's west bank before dusk and let the Mekong, small islands and reflected evening light do the rest.
thing-don-det-sunset.gettingThere: Walk or bicycle to the west / sunset side of Don Det

thing-tad-hang-waterfall.description: Walk from Tad Lo to Tad Hang, a broad tiered Xe Set cascade beside the village, then decide between a riverside pause and a cautious swim according to the day’s water conditions.
thing-tad-hang-waterfall.gettingThere: About 700 m by road from Tad Lo Tourism Office; easy on foot
thing-tad-hang-waterfall.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon; check swimming conditions after rain

thing-tad-lo-waterfall.description: Walk upstream through Tad Lo to the village’s namesake waterfall, a broad Xe Set cascade framed by trees and river paths, then pair it with Tad Hang rather than treating the two falls as separate excursions.
thing-tad-lo-waterfall.gettingThere: About 1.1 km by road from Tad Lo Tourism Office; walkable through the village
thing-tad-lo-waterfall.bestTime: Morning or late afternoon; check river conditions after rain

thing-tad-soung-waterfall.description: Follow the rural road from Tad Lo through fields and villages to Tad Soung, then choose the lower-to-upper trail or the longer road approach for a high escarpment and wide valley panorama.
thing-tad-soung-waterfall.gettingThere: About 4 km by road to the lower falls; climb the renovated trail or continue roughly 4 km farther by road to the upper access
thing-tad-soung-waterfall.bestTime: Morning; wet season for stronger flow, dry season still worthwhile for the panorama

thing-katu-weaving-workshop.description: Spend a half day learning Katu weaving with a local host, from the body tension of a foot-braced backstrap loom to the patience behind woven bead patterns.
thing-katu-weaving-workshop.gettingThere: Walkable from Tad Lo; confirm the exact host and meeting point when booking
thing-katu-weaving-workshop.bestTime: By arrangement; book ahead, with lower availability possible in low season

thing-lao-cooking-class-with-nyay.description: Cook a Lao meal with Nyay in a relaxed half-day workshop, using fresh local ingredients before sitting down to eat the dishes you prepared together.
thing-lao-cooking-class-with-nyay.gettingThere: Walkable in Tad Lo; confirm the exact meeting point when booking
thing-lao-cooking-class-with-nyay.bestTime: Morning class for lunch or afternoon class for dinner; book ahead

thing-coffee-and-katu-culture-with-mr-ho.description: Ride about 15 km from Tad Lo to Ban Kok Phoung Tai for a roughly three-hour guided visit with Mr Hook combining coffee, useful plants and a direct conversation about Katu culture and change.
thing-coffee-and-katu-culture-with-mr-ho.gettingThere: About 15 km by road from Tad Lo Tourism Office to Ban Kok Phoung Tai; motorbike recommended, car or minivan possible
thing-coffee-and-katu-culture-with-mr-ho.bestTime: By arrangement; confirm current departure time, price and availability before going

thing-coffee-from-tree-to-cup-with-mr-vi.description: Ride out toward Laongam for a compact coffee-farm visit with Mr Vieng, following the crop from trees and ripe cherries through processing and preparation before finishing with coffee grown on the farm.
thing-coffee-from-tree-to-cup-with-mr-vi.gettingThere: About 30 km by road from Tad Lo Tourism Office near Laongam; motorbike recommended, car or minivan possible
thing-coffee-from-tree-to-cup-with-mr-vi.bestTime: By arrangement; confirm current visit time, price and booking method before leaving Tad Lo
